trust_section_content: Home Nura is an independent guide to air fryers, based in Europe, published for Europe and North America and launched in 2024. Our methodology rests on five transparent criteria: cooking quality, value for money, ease of use, energy use and design. Every shortlisted model is evaluated using manufacturer spec sheets, cross-checked verified buyer reviews (Amazon, Google) and tests published by specialist media. The Nura Score, out of 10, weights and combines these criteria. Our only source of revenue is the Amazon Associates program, disclosed on every link: no manufacturer can buy a better score, and our rankings remain strictly independent.
market_section_title: The air fryer market in 2026: a look at France
market_section_content: France's air fryer market is booming. In 2026, more than 35% of French households own at least one air fryer, up from 18% in 2022, and the category brings in more than €480 million a year. Philips leads with a 30% market share, followed by Ninja (22%), Cosori (15%), Moulinex (12%), Tefal (10%) and other brands (11%). In France, prices run from €49 for entry-level models to more than €600 for high-end machines, but most French shoppers buy in the €150 to €350 range, where the best-quality models are concentrated. Key trends include strong demand for smart models (38% of sales), XXL sizes for large families (up 42% a year) and dual-basket designs (a 26% share). French kitchens, long attached to traditional cooking, are gradually turning to air fryers for their energy efficiency and versatility.
testing_section_content: We don't test products ourselves. We compare every air fryer using three sources: manufacturer spec sheets, cross-checked verified buyer reviews (Amazon, Google) and tests published by specialist media. We analyze that data against five criteria: cooking quality, value for money, ease of use, energy use and design. The Nura Score, out of 10, weights and combines these criteria so every model is compared on the same basis. No manufacturer can buy a better score.
recommendation_section_title: Quick guide: Which air fryer is right for you?
recommendation_section_content: Just starting out? In the under-$150 tier, the 2.7-quart (2.6 L) Cosori Lite and the 4.2-quart (4 L) Tefal Compact offer the best value, with solid performance and intuitive controls that suit first-time buyers. Large household (5+ people)? Go for an XXL model such as the 5.5-quart (5.2 L) Ninja AF500 or the Philips 6L XL (6.3 qt), which handle family meals with ease, and pick a dual-basket design if you want to cook two dishes at once. Tech-savvy and want app control? The Wi-Fi-enabled Ninja Foodi Smart and the Philips Connected range offer full smartphone control, smart presets and a cooking history. Want a lower energy bill? The Cosori Pro (1,500 W) and Tefal Precision (1,400 W) use 15% to 20% less power than the average model while keeping excellent heat performance. Sensitive to noise? The Philips Compact (under 70 dB) and the Ninja Whisper Series run quietly, ideal for open-concept kitchens. Working with a tight budget, under $90? In that tier, the 2.1-quart (2 L) Cecotec Compact and the 1.9-quart (1.8 L) Costway Ultra cover the basics without major compromises on cooking quality.
guide_intro_title: How to choose the best air fryer in 2026
guide_intro_text: Air fryers keep winning over home cooks, and choosing between Ninja, Philips, Cosori, Moulinex and Tefal models isn't easy. Our comparison guide helps you find the right air fryer for your budget, household size and cooking habits.
guide_criteria_title: What to look for in an air fryer
guide_criteria_capacity: Capacity: about 2 to 3 quarts (2–3 L) for one or two people, 4 to 5 quarts (4–5 L) for three or four, and 6 quarts (6 L) or more for large families. Dual-basket models let you cook two dishes at the same time.
guide_criteria_power: Power: 1,000 to 2,200 W. The higher the wattage, the faster the preheat; models rated 1,400 to 1,800 W strike the best balance. Models sold in Europe are built for 230 V, so check that the version on your Amazon store is rated for 120 V.
guide_criteria_features: Features: preset cooking programs, Wi-Fi, a timer and a keep-warm setting. Smart models let you control everything from your phone.

faq.question: How does an air fryer work?
faq.answer: An air fryer uses a powerful fan to circulate very hot air around the food, giving it a crisp finish similar to deep frying with up to 80% less fat. Rapid Air technology spreads the heat evenly for consistent results every time.

faq.question: What size air fryer do I need for my family?
faq.answer: For one or two people, a 2- to 3-quart (2–3 L) model is enough. For a family of three or four, go for 4 to 5 quarts (4–5 L). For five or more people, choose an extra-large model of 6 quarts (6 L) or more. Dual-basket models let you cook two dishes at the same time, which is handy for busy households.

faq.question: Do air fryers use a lot of electricity?
faq.answer: No. Air fryers are very energy efficient. They typically draw 1,000 to 1,700 W and cook faster than a conventional oven, cutting energy use by 30% to 50%. With regular use (four or five meals a week), that can save about $45 to $55 a year on your electric bill at an example rate of 20 cents per kWh; check the rate on your utility bill.

faq.question: Can you cook frozen food in an air fryer?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Air fryers do a great job with frozen foods: fries, chicken nuggets, onion rings, breaded vegetables. There's no need to thaw them first. Cooking time is typically 20% shorter than in an oven, and the results come out crispier.

faq.question: What's the difference between an air fryer and a convection oven?
faq.answer: An air fryer is essentially a compact, concentrated convection oven. Its smaller cavity allows more intense airflow and almost instant preheating. The result: faster cooking, crispier food and lower energy use than a full-size oven.

faq.question: Which air fryer is best for a family of four?
faq.answer: For a family of four, we recommend an air fryer with a capacity of about 4 to 6 quarts (4–6 L). The 6.8-quart (6.4 L) Cosori Dual Blaze offers outstanding value, with dual heating elements that deliver perfectly even browning. The 6.6-quart (6.2 L) Philips Airfryer 3000 XL is another excellent choice, thanks to its proven reliability and Rapid Air technology. For families who regularly cook big batches, the 10-quart (9.5 L) Ninja Foodi MAX Double Stack lets you make two completely different dishes at the same time. Plan on a budget of $150 to $300 for a model that performs well and lasts.

faq.question: How much does a good air fryer cost in 2026?
faq.answer: In 2026, air fryer prices vary widely with features and capacity. The entry-level tier ($70 to $100), with models such as the Cosori Lite and Tefal Compact, suits beginners and small kitchens. The midrange tier ($150 to $250) offers the best value, with models such as the Philips 3000 XL and Cosori Dual Blaze. The premium tier ($300 to $450), with models such as the Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer and Philips Combi XXL Connected, adds Wi-Fi, extra-large capacities and advanced cooking functions. Our advice: budget $100 to $250 for a high-performing model that should last five years or more.

faq.question: How do you clean an air fryer properly?
faq.answer: Regular cleaning keeps your air fryer performing well and extends its life. After each use, let it cool for 10 to 15 minutes. Remove the basket and drawer, then wash them in warm, soapy water or put them in the dishwasher (check your manual to make sure they're dishwasher-safe). For stubborn residue, soak them for 15 minutes in warm water with baking soda. Wipe the inside of the unit with a damp cloth — never submerge the main body in water. To get rid of lingering odors, run the air fryer empty for 5 minutes with half a lemon in the basket. A thorough deep clean once a month can add 2 to 3 years to your appliance's life.

faq.question: How much electricity does an air fryer really use?
faq.answer: Much less than a traditional oven. A standard air fryer draws between 800 and 1,800 W, and midrange models average around 1,400 W. A conventional oven, by comparison, uses 2,000 to 3,000 W. Based on manufacturers' rated power, an air fryer uses roughly 0.7 kWh to cook a full meal (fries and chicken for four), compared with 1.8 kWh for the same meal in an oven. With regular use (four or five times a week over a year), that saves about $45 to $55 on your electric bill at an example rate of 20 cents per kWh; check the rate on your utility bill. The most efficient models in our comparison are the Xiaomi Smart Air Fryer Pro (800 W) and, for smaller portions, the Cosori Lite (900 W).

faq.question: Can you bake cakes and pastries in an air fryer?
faq.answer: Yes, air fryers are surprisingly good at baking. You can make muffins, brownies, cookies, small cakes and even bread. The trick is to lower the temperature by about 35°F (20°C) compared with a standard oven recipe and keep a closer eye on the bake, since the circulating hot air speeds things up. Use silicone molds or paper liners that fit your basket. Models with a flat base, such as the Philips Combi XXL, are best suited to baking. Common starting points: brownies at 300°F (150°C) for 15 minutes, muffins at 320°F (160°C) for 12 minutes and cookies at 320°F (160°C) for 8 minutes. The result: soft and moist inside, crisp outside, with almost no preheating time.

faq.question: Air fryer vs. deep fryer: What's the difference?
faq.answer: The fundamental difference is the cooking method. A traditional deep fryer submerges food in 2 to 3 quarts (2–3 L) of hot oil at about 350°F (175°C), while an air fryer circulates very hot air at high speed. In practice, air-fried fries are slightly less crispy than deep-fried ones but contain up to 80% less fat. Health-wise, air frying sharply reduces acrylamide, a potentially carcinogenic compound that forms during high-temperature frying. Air fryers are also safer (no hot oil splattering), much easier to clean and far more versatile — you can roast, broil and reheat, too. For an authentic deep-fried result, though, like Belgian-style fries, a traditional fryer still wins.

faq.question: Are air fryers really healthier?
faq.answer: Yes. Air fryers offer real health benefits backed by scientific research. The main one is the 70% to 80% cut in fat: air-fried fries contain about 4 g of fat, compared with 17 g for deep-fried fries (per 7-oz, or 200 g, serving). Hot-air cooking also reduces acrylamide formation by up to 90% compared with deep frying, according to research published in the Journal of Food Science. And because cooking times are shorter, air fryers preserve more of the vitamins and nutrients in food. That said, ultra-processed foods stay ultra-processed whatever the cooking method: air-fried frozen nuggets are still processed food. For the best results, use your air fryer with fresh, whole ingredients.

faq.question: How long does an air fryer last?
faq.answer: Based on verified buyer reviews and published tests, a quality air fryer lasts 5 to 8 years on average with regular care. The key factors in longevity are the quality of the nonstick coating (ceramic models tend to outlast Teflon), the sturdiness of the drawer mechanism and the quality of the heating element. In our comparisons, Philips and Ninja consistently score highest for durability, based on owner feedback over several years of use. To get the most out of yours, clean it after every use, avoid metal utensils on the nonstick surface and never fill the basket beyond its recommended capacity.

faq.question: What's the best budget air fryer in 2026?
faq.answer: The best budget air fryer of 2026 is the 4-quart (3.8 L) Cosori Lite, which earns an impressive Nura Score of 7.8/10 despite its affordable price. It offers 1,500 W of power, four presets and a basket big enough for two or three people. In second place, the 4.2-quart (4 L) Xiaomi Smart Air Fryer Pro stands out with Wi-Fi and control through the Mi Home app — a rare luxury in this price range. The 5.3-quart (5 L) Moulinex Easy Fry Max offers the largest capacity in the budget tier. Our criteria for budget models (under $100): proven reliability, a durable nonstick coating, easy cleaning and reasonable energy use. In the EU, all of these models carry at least a two-year guarantee; for the version you buy, check the manufacturer's warranty.

faq.question: How is the Nura Score calculated?
faq.answer: The Nura Score is our rating system: a score out of 10 based on five weighted criteria. We don't test products ourselves; each score draws on manufacturer spec sheets, cross-checked verified buyer reviews (Amazon, Google) and tests published by specialist media. Cooking quality (30%): crispiness, even browning and versatility, as reported in verified reviews and published tests. Value for money (25%): reported performance relative to the price in each European market. Ease of use (15%): controls, preset programs, cleaning, basket design and display readability. Energy use (15%): rated power, preheat time and published consumption data. Design (15%): materials, build quality, footprint and durability as reported by buyers. The Nura Score is updated quarterly to reflect long-term owner feedback.
